preface.p: Measures to Combat Serious and Organised Crime Act 2001
This is a compilation of the Measures to Combat Serious and Organised Crime Act 2001 that shows the text of the law as amended and in force on 27 August 2026 (the compilation date).
The notes at the end of this compilation (the endnotes) include information about amending laws and the amendment history of provisions of the compiled law.

The effect of uncommenced amendments is not shown in the text of the compiled law. The details of amendments made up to, but not commenced at, the compilation date are underlined in the endnotes. Any uncommenced amendments affecting the law are accessible on the Register (www.legislation.gov.au).

If the operation of a provision or amendment of the compiled law is affected by an application, saving or transitional provision that is not included in this compilation, details are included in the endnotes.
For more information about any editorial changes made in this compilation, see the endnotes.

The Legislation Act 2003 provides for First Parliamentary Counsel to make presentational changes to a compilation. Presentational changes are applied to give a more consistent look and feel to legislation published on the Register, and enable the user to more easily navigate those documents.

If the compiled law is modified by another law, the compiled law operates as modified but the modification does not amend the text of the law. Accordingly, this compilation does not show the text of the compiled law as modified. Any modifications affecting the law are accessible on the Register.
If a provision of the compiled law has been repealed in accordance with a provision of the law, details are included in the endnotes.

section.heading: Commencement

content.p: This section and sections 1 and 3 commence on the day on which this Act receives the Royal Assent.

section.heading: What is a controlled operation?

content.p: A controlled operation is an operation that:
involves the participation of law enforcement officers; and
is carried out for the purpose of obtaining evidence that may lead to the prosecution of a person for a serious Commonwealth offence; and

may involve a law enforcement officer or other person in acts, or omissions to act, that would, apart from subsection 15I(1) or (3), constitute a Commonwealth offence or an offence against a law of a State or Territory.

section.heading: Meaning of engage in conduct etc.

content.p: In this Part:
a reference to engaging in conduct includes a reference to omitting to act; and
a reference to a person’s conduct includes a reference to the person’s omissions.

section.heading: What is a serious Commonwealth offence?

content.p: For the purposes of this Part, serious Commonwealth offence means an offence against a law of the Commonwealth:

that involves theft, fraud, tax evasion, currency violations, illegal drug dealings, illegal gambling, obtaining financial benefit by vice engaged in by others, extortion, money laundering, perverting the course of justice, bribery or corruption of, or by, an officer of the Commonwealth, an officer of a State or an officer of a Territory, bankruptcy and company violations, harbouring of criminals, forgery including forging of passports, armament dealings, illegal importation or exportation of fauna into or out of Australia, espionage, sabotage or threats to national security, misuse of a computer or electronic communications, people smuggling, slavery, piracy, the organisation, financing or perpetration of sexual servitude or child sex tourism, dealings in child pornography or material depicting child abuse, importation of prohibited imports or exportation of prohibited exports, or that involves matters of the same general nature as one or more of the foregoing or that is of any other prescribed kind; and
that is punishable on conviction by imprisonment for a period of 3 years or more.

section.heading: Law enforcement officers etc. not liable for offences committed for purposes of authorised controlled operation

content.p: A law enforcement officer who engages in conduct that, apart from this subsection, would constitute a Commonwealth offence or an offence against a law of a State or Territory is not criminally responsible for that offence if:
he or she engages in that conduct in the course of duty for the purposes of a controlled operation; and
the conduct meets the requirements of subsection 15IB(1).

A person who is not a law enforcement officer and who engages in conduct that, apart from this subsection, would constitute a Commonwealth offence or an offence against a law of a State or Territory is not criminally responsible for that offence if:
he or she engages in that conduct for the purposes of a controlled operation; and
a law enforcement officer has authorised the person to engage in that conduct; and
the conduct meets the requirements of subsection 15IB(2).
Subsection (2) does not apply to a person who:
is an informant of a law enforcement officer; or
is believed to have been involved, other than for law enforcement purposes, in the criminal activity in respect of which the controlled operation was authorised.

The fact that, because of subsection (1) or (2), a person whose conduct is covered by a certificate given under section 15M is not criminally responsible for an offence does not affect the liability, for that offence or any other offence, of any person whose conduct is not covered by the certificate.
(4) Subsection (3) applies despite any provision of Chapter 2 of the Criminal Code to the contrary.

section.heading: Indemnification of law enforcement officers etc.

content.p: The Commonwealth must indemnify a law enforcement officer against any liability (including reasonable costs) the officer incurs because of conduct the officer engages in if:
he or she engages in that conduct in the course of duty for the purposes of a controlled operation; and
the conduct meets the requirements of subsection 15IB(1); and
the requirements (if any) specified in the regulations have been met.
The Commonwealth must indemnify a person who is not a law enforcement officer against any liability (including reasonable costs) the person incurs because of conduct the person engages in if:
he or she engages in that conduct for the purposes of a controlled operation; and
a law enforcement officer has authorised the person to engage in that conduct; and
the conduct meets the requirements of subsection 15IB(2); and
the requirements (if any) specified in the regulations have been met.
Subsection (2) does not apply to a person who:
is an informant of a law enforcement officer; or
is believed to have been involved, other than for law enforcement purposes, in the criminal activity in respect of which the controlled operation was authorised.

For the purposes of this section, a member of a police force or other law enforcement agency of a foreign country is taken to be acting in the course of duty to the extent that he or she takes part in the controlled operation in accordance with the instructions given by an Australian law enforcement officer.

section.heading: Requirements that must be met for the purposes of sections 15I and 15IA

content.p: A law enforcement officer’s conduct relating to a controlled operation meets the requirements of this subsection if:
at the time when he or she engages in that conduct there is in force a certificate given under section 15M that authorises the operation; and
the conduct is within the nature of the activities covered by the certificate; and
the conduct does not breach any conditions to which the certificate is subject; and

the conduct does not involve intentionally inducing a person to commit a Commonwealth offence, or an offence against a law of a State or Territory, if that person would not otherwise have intended to commit:
that offence; or
an offence of that kind; and
the conduct does not involve the commission of a sexual offence against any person or an offence involving the death of or serious injury to any person.
Any other person’s conduct relating to a controlled operation meets the requirements of this subsection if:
at the time when he or she engages in that conduct there is in force a certificate given under section 15M that authorises the operation; and
the certificate identifies the person as being permitted to be involved in the operation; and
the conduct is within the nature of the activities covered by the certificate; and
the conduct does not breach any conditions to which the certificate is subject; and

the conduct does not involve intentionally inducing a person to commit a Commonwealth offence, or an offence against a law of a State or Territory, if that person would not otherwise have intended to commit:
that offence; or
an offence of that kind; and
the conduct does not involve the commission of a sexual offence against any person or an offence involving the death of or serious injury to any person.

section.heading: Effect of sections 15I and 15IA on other laws relating to criminal investigation

content.p: Sections 15I and 15IA do not apply to a person’s conduct that is authorised, or could have been authorised, under a law of the Commonwealth, a State or a Territory relating to:
arrest or detention of individuals; or
searches of individuals; or
entry onto, or searches or inspections of, premises; or
searches, inspections or seizures of other property; or
forensic procedures; or
electronic surveillance devices or telecommunications interception; or
identification procedures; or
any other matter concerning powers of criminal investigation.

section.heading: Compensation for loss or injury

content.p: Where a person suffers loss or injury as a result of a controlled operation, the Commonwealth is liable to pay to the person who has suffered the loss or injury such compensation as is agreed on between the Commonwealth and that person or, in default of agreement, is determined by action against the Commonwealth in a court of competent jurisdiction.

foreign officer means an officer, however described, of an agency that has responsibility for: law enforcement in a foreign country; or intelligence gathering for a foreign country; or security of a foreign country.
law enforcement in a foreign country; or
intelligence gathering for a foreign country; or
security of a foreign country.
issuing agency means:
a Commonwealth agency; or
a non-government body;
that is referred to in an authorisation under paragraph 15XI(2)(f).
issuing evidence of an assumed identity includes making an entry in a record of information in respect of the assumed identity.
non-government body means a body that is not managed or controlled by or on behalf of the Commonwealth or the Government of a State or Territory.
participating agency means either a Commonwealth participating agency or a State or Territory participating agency.
State or Territory participating agency means:
the police force of a State or Territory; or
one of the following bodies:
(i) the Independent Commission Against Corruption established under the Independent Commission Against Corruption Act 1988 of New South Wales;
(ii) the Queensland Criminal Justice Commission established by the Criminal Justice Act 1989 of Queensland;
(iii) the Western Australian Anti-Corruption Commission established by the Anti-Corruption Act 1988 of Western Australia;
a similar body established under a law of a State or Territory; or
one of the following bodies:
(i) the New South Wales Crime Commission established under the New South Wales Crime Commission Act 1985 of New South Wales;
(ii) the Queensland Crime Commission established by the Crime Commission Act 1997 of Queensland;
a similar body established under a law of a State or Territory; or
(ca) the Police Integrity Commission established by the Police Integrity Commission Act 1996 of New South Wales; or
(d) any other body or agency of a State or Territory specified in the regulations.
supervising officer means the officer referred to in an authorisation under subparagraph 15XI(2)(d)(ii).
A reference in this Part to an approved officer or an approved person using an assumed identity includes a reference to:

the officer or person representing the identity covered by his or her authorisation to be his or her real identity when it is not (whether that representation is express or implied, and whether it is by words, conduct or omission); or
such an officer or person acting in a way that is consistent with such an identity, rather than the person’s real identity.

A reference in this Part to an approved officer or approved person acquiring evidence of an assumed identity includes a reference to the officer or person obtaining, or taking any steps towards obtaining, a document or other thing that purports to evidence the identity covered by his or her authorisation, when it is not the real identity of the person.
A reference in this Part to a person engaging in conduct includes a reference to the person omitting to do an act.

section.heading: Assumed identities may be acquired and used

content.p: An approved officer may acquire evidence of, and use, an assumed identity if the acquisition or use:
is in the course of duty; and
is in accordance with the authorisation conditions (if any).
An approved person may acquire evidence of, and use, an assumed identity if the acquisition or use is in accordance with:
directions given by the supervising officer mentioned in the person’s authorisation; and
the authorisation conditions (if any).
Note: The acquisition of evidence, and use, of an assumed identity is authorised by the authorising person of a participating agency under Division 3.

section.heading: Protection from criminal liability

content.p: An approved officer, who engages in conduct that, apart from this subsection, would constitute an offence against a law of the Commonwealth, a State or Territory, is not criminally responsible for that offence if:
the officer engages in the conduct in the course of acquiring evidence of, or using, an assumed identity; and
the officer engages in the conduct in the course of duty; and
the conduct is in accordance with the authorisation conditions (if any); and
the conduct would not constitute that offence if the assumed identity were the officer’s real identity.

Example: This subsection could apply if an approved officer, when using an assumed identity, makes the false representation that he or she is unemployed (but that representation would be true if the assumed identity were real).

An approved person who engages in conduct that, apart from this subsection, would constitute an offence against a law of the Commonwealth, a State or Territory, is not criminally responsible for that offence if:
the person engages in the conduct in the course of acquiring evidence of, or using, an assumed identity; and
the conduct is in accordance with:
directions given by the supervising officer; and
the authorisation conditions (if any); and
the conduct would not constitute that offence if the assumed identity were the person’s real identity.
Note: Division 5 has offences relating to the misuse etc. of assumed identities.

section.heading: Indemnification of approved officers and persons

content.p: A Commonwealth participating agency whose authorising person issues an authorisation must indemnify an approved officer against any liability (including reasonable costs) that the officer incurs because of conduct the officer engages in if:
the officer is covered by the authorisation; and
the officer engages in the conduct in acquiring evidence of, or using, an assumed identity in the course of duty; and
the conduct is in accordance with the authorisation conditions (if any); and
the requirements (if any) specified in the regulations have been met.

A Commonwealth participating agency whose authorising person issues an authorisation must indemnify an approved person against any liability (including reasonable costs) that the person incurs because of conduct the person engages in if:
the person is covered by an authorisation; and
the person engages in conduct in acquiring evidence of, or using, an assumed identity; and
the conduct is in accordance with:
any directions given by the supervising officer; and
the authorisation conditions (if any); and
the requirements (if any) specified in the regulations have been met.

section.heading: Effect of being unaware of variation or revocation of authorisation

content.p: If an approved officer’s or approved person’s authorisation has been varied in a way that limits its scope, this Division continues to apply to the officer or person, as if the authorisation had not been varied in that way, for so long as he or she:
is unaware of the variation; and
is not reckless with respect to the existence of the variation.

If an approved officer’s or approved person’s authorisation is revoked, this Division continues to apply to the officer or person, as if the authorisation had not been revoked, for so long as he or she:
is unaware of the revocation; and
is not reckless with respect to the existence of the revocation.
For the purposes of this section, a person is reckless with respect to the variation or revocation of an authorisation if:
he or she is aware of a substantial risk that the variation or revocation occurred; and
having regard to the circumstances known to him or her, it is unjustifiable to take the risk.

section.heading: Documents authorising use of skill or qualification

content.p: Sections 15XC and 15XD do not apply to an approved officer or approved person engaging in conduct if:
a particular skill or qualification is needed to engage in that conduct; and
the person does not have that skill or qualification;
whether or not the officer or person has acquired, as evidence of an assumed identity, a document that establishes that he or she has that skill or qualification.
Example: An officer who cannot fly a plane is not authorised to fly even though he or she has acquired a pilot’s licence under an assumed identity.

division.heading: Authorising the acquisition or use of assumed identities

section.heading: Commonwealth authorisations of the acquisition or use of assumed identities

content.p: An authorising person of a Commonwealth participating agency may, if satisfied that it is appropriate to do so, authorise a person to do either or both of the following:
acquire evidence of an assumed identity from:
any Commonwealth agency; or
any non-government body;
use the assumed identity.
However, the authorising person may only authorise the use of the assumed identity in a foreign country if he or she is satisfied that it is reasonably necessary to do so.
An authorising person of a Commonwealth participating agency may, if satisfied that it is reasonably necessary to do so, authorise a foreign officer to do either or both of the following:
acquire evidence of an assumed identity from:
any Commonwealth agency; or
any non-government body;
use an assumed identity.

section.heading: State or Territory authorisations of the acquisition or use of assumed identities

content.p: An authorising person of a State or Territory participating agency may, if satisfied that it is appropriate to do so, authorise a person (other than a foreign officer) to do either or both of the following:
acquire evidence of an assumed identity from any Commonwealth agency;
use the assumed identity.
Note: Only a Commonwealth participating agency can authorise a foreign officer to acquire evidence of, or use, an assumed identity: see subsection 15XG(3).
However, the authorising person may only authorise the use of the assumed identity in a foreign country if he or she is satisfied that it is reasonably necessary to do so.

section.heading: Contents of an authorisation for an assumed identity

content.p: (1) An authorisation to acquire evidence of, and use, an assumed identity must be in writing and signed by the authorising person.
The authorisation must specify:
the authorising person’s name; and
the date on which the authorisation is given; and
if the person who is authorised to acquire or use the assumed identity is an officer in the authorising person’s participating agency or a foreign officer—that officer’s name; and
if the person who is authorised to acquire or use the assumed identity is not such an officer:
the name of the person who is authorised to acquire or use the assumed identity; and
(ii) the name of the officer in the authorising person’s participating agency who will supervise that acquisition or use; and
details of the assumed identity which the authorisation covers; and
all Commonwealth agencies or non-government bodies who are to be requested to issue evidence of the assumed identity; and
details of each such request; and
the reasons for the need to use the assumed identity; and
whether the assumed identity can be used in a foreign country and the reasons for the need for this use; and
any conditions to which the authorisation is subject, including in relation to use in a foreign country.
An authorisation can cover more than one assumed identity.

section.heading: When an authorisation is in force

content.p: An authorisation is in force until it is revoked.

section.heading: Variation and revocation of authorisations

content.p: An authorising person who issues an authorisation, or any other authorising person in the same participating agency, may vary or revoke the authorisation at any time.
(2) The approved officer or approved person covered by the authorisation must be given a written notice of the variation or revocation.
The notice must state:
the date from which the variation or revocation takes effect; and
the nature of the variation (if any); and
the reasons for the variation or revocation.

division.heading: Issuing and cancelling evidence of assumed identities

section.heading: Authorising person may request agencies and bodies to issue evidence of assumed identities etc.

content.p: An authorising person who issues an authorisation may request an issuing agency that is specified in the authorisation under paragraph 15XI(2)(f) to issue evidence of an assumed identity covered by the authorisation to the approved officer or approved person.

section.heading: Requesting Commonwealth agencies to issue evidence of assumed identities etc.

content.p: (1) An issuing agency of the Commonwealth that receives a request under section 15XL from an authorising person in a Commonwealth participating agency must comply with the request.
An issuing agency of the Commonwealth that receives such a request from an authorising person in a State or Territory participating agency may comply with the request, but does not have to do so.

section.heading: Requesting non-government bodies to issue evidence of assumed identities etc.

content.p: An issuing agency that is a non-government body that receives a request under section 15XL may comply with the request, but does not have to do so.
Note: Only Commonwealth participating agencies can request non-government bodies to issue evidence of an assumed identity.

section.heading: Cancelling evidence of assumed identities etc.

content.p: An issuing agency that has issued evidence of an assumed identity because of a request under section 15XL, must cancel the evidence (including by deleting or altering an entry in a record of information) on the written request of:
the authorising person who made the request; or
any other authorising person in the same participating agency.

section.heading: Protection from criminal liability

content.p: An employee in an issuing agency, who engages in conduct that, apart from this section, would constitute an offence against a law of the Commonwealth, a State or Territory, is not criminally responsible for the offence if the employee engages in the conduct in responding to the request in the course of duty.

section.heading: Indemnification of issuing agencies etc.

content.p: A Commonwealth participating agency whose authorising person makes a request under section 15XL must indemnify:
an employee of an issuing agency; and
(b) an issuing agency;
against any liability (including reasonable costs) incurred by that employee or agency because of conduct engaged in by the employee if:
the employee engages in the conduct in responding to the request in the course of duty; and
the requirements (if any) specified in the regulations have been met.

section.heading: Misuse of assumed identities

content.p: A person commits an offence if:
the person is an approved officer; and
the person acquires evidence of, or uses, an assumed identity covered by the person’s authorisation; and
the acquisition or use is not in the course of duty.
Penalty: 12 months imprisonment.
A person commits an offence if:
the person is an approved person; and
the person acquires evidence of, or uses, an assumed identity covered by the person’s authorisation; and
the acquisition or use is not in accordance with the directions of the supervising officer.
Penalty: 12 months imprisonment.
A person commits an offence if:
the person is an approved officer or an approved person; and
the person acquires evidence of, or uses, an assumed identity covered by the person’s authorisation; and
in doing so, the person engages in conduct that breaches an authorisation condition.
Penalty: 12 months imprisonment.

section.heading: Disclosing information relating to assumed identities

content.p: A person commits an offence if:
the person discloses information; and
the disclosure reveals, or is likely to reveal, that an assumed identity acquired or used by another person is not that other person’s real identity; and
the disclosure:
endangers, or is likely to endanger, the health or safety of any person; or
prejudices, or is likely to prejudice, the effective conduct of an operation carried out by any participating agency; and
the assumed identity is or was covered by an authorisation.
Penalty: 10 years imprisonment.
A person commits an offence if:
the person discloses information; and
the disclosure reveals, or is likely to reveal, that an assumed identity acquired or used by another person is not that other person’s real identity; and
the assumed identity is or was covered by an authorisation.
Penalty: 2 years imprisonment.

section.heading: Disclosing real identities during court proceedings etc.

content.p: If the real identity of an approved officer or approved person who is or was covered by an authorisation, might be disclosed in proceedings before a court, tribunal or a Royal Commission or other commission of inquiry, then the court, tribunal or commission must:
ensure that the parts of the proceedings that relate to the real identity of the officer or person are held in private; and

make such orders relating to the suppression of the publication of evidence given by the court, tribunal or commission as will, in its opinion, ensure that the real identity of the officer or person is not disclosed.
However, this section does not apply to the extent that the court, tribunal or commission considers that the interests of justice require otherwise.

section.heading: Keeping and auditing records of assumed identities

content.p: The head of a Commonwealth participating agency must:
cause appropriate records to be kept:
while an authorisation is in force; and
for at least 12 months after an authorisation has been revoked; and
cause those records to be audited:
(i) at least once every 6 months while the authorisation is in force; and
at least once in the 6 month period after the revocation of the authorisation.
An audit of these records must not be conducted by:
an authorising person who has issued, varied or revoked an authorisation to which one or more of the records relate; or
an approved officer or approved person who is covered by an authorisation to which one or more of the records relate.
In this section:

appropriate records means records relating to the operation of this Part as it affects the participating agency, including any authorisations and any variations or revocations of those authorisations under section 15XK.

section.heading: Matters to be reported

content.p: Commonwealth participating agencies must report annually
Each of the following Commonwealth participating agencies:
the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation;
the Australian Secret Intelligence Service;
must, as soon as practicable after 30 June in each year, prepare and give to the Inspector-General of Intelligence and Security a report for the year ending on that 30 June.

Each other Commonwealth participating agency must, within 3 months after 30 June in each year, prepare and give to the Minister responsible for the agency a report for the year ending on that 30 June.

The Minister receiving a report under subsection (2) must table a copy of the report before each House of the Parliament within 15 sitting days of that House after the day on which the Minister receives the report.
What reports must include
An agency’s report must include the following information:
the number of authorisations issued by an authorising person from the agency during the year covered by the report;
a general description of the activities undertaken by approved officers and approved persons when using their assumed identities during the year covered by the report;
a statement whether or not any fraud or other unlawful activity was identified by an audit under paragraph 15XU(1)(b) during the year covered by the report.
Before the report is tabled in the Parliament, the Minister must, on the advice of the relevant agency head, remove information from the report if the Minister is of the view that its inclusion may:
endanger a person’s safety; or
prejudice an investigation or prosecution; or
compromise the agency’s operational activities or methodologies.

section.heading: Concurrent operation of State and Territory laws

content.p: It is the Parliament’s intention that a law of a State or Territory should be able to operate concurrently with this Part unless the law is directly inconsistent with this Part.

section.heading: Regulations

content.p: The Governor-General may make regulations prescribing matters:
required or permitted by this Part to be prescribed; or
necessary or convenient to be prescribed for carrying out or giving effect to this Part.

part.heading: Protection of children in proceedings for sexual offences

section.heading: Proceedings to which this Part applies

content.p: This Part applies to any proceedings for:
an offence against Part IIIA of this Act (Child sex tourism); or
(b) an offence against section 71.8 of the Criminal Code (Sexual assault of United Nations and associated personnel); or
(c) an offence against Division 270 of the Criminal Code (Slavery, sexual servitude and deceptive recruiting); or
a sexual offence specified in the regulations; or
an offence that includes the commission of, or the intention to commit, an offence of a kind referred to in paragraph (a), (b), (c) or (d); or
an offence of:
attempting to commit; or
conspiring to commit; or
inciting the commission of;
an offence of a kind referred to in paragraph (a), (b), (c), (d) or (e).
This Part also applies to any proceedings, including committal proceedings or proceedings of a similar kind, connected with proceedings of a kind referred to in subsection (1).

section.heading: Definitions

content.p: In this Part, unless the contrary intention appears:
child means a person who is under 18.

child complainant, in relation to a proceeding, means a child who is, or is alleged to be, a victim of an offence, of a kind referred to in subsection 15Y(1), to which the proceeding relates. The child need not be involved in the proceeding or the initiation of the proceeding.
child witness, in relation to a proceeding, means a child (including a child complainant) who is a witness in the proceeding.
closed-circuit television includes any similar technology specified in the regulations.
credibility has the meaning given by the Evidence Act 1995.
cross-examination has the meaning given by the Evidence Act 1995.
evidence in chief means evidence given in examination in chief within the meaning of the Evidence Act 1995.
proceeding means a proceeding to which this Part applies under section 15Y.

section.heading: Evidence of sexual reputation

content.p: Evidence of a child witness’ or child complainant’s reputation with respect to sexual activities is inadmissible in a proceeding, unless the court gives leave.
The court must not give leave unless satisfied that the evidence is substantially relevant to facts in issue in the proceeding.
The evidence is not to be treated as substantially relevant to facts in issue merely because of inferences it may raise as to the child witness’ or child complainant’s general disposition.
If the evidence is admitted, it must not be treated as relevant to the child witness’ or child complainant’s credibility.
This section does not apply if the child is a defendant in the proceeding.

section.heading: Evidence of sexual experience

content.p: Evidence of a child witness’ or child complainant’s experience with respect to sexual activities is inadmissible in a proceeding, unless:
the court gives leave; or
the evidence is of sexual activities with a defendant in the proceeding.
The court must not give leave unless satisfied that:
the evidence is substantially relevant to facts in issue in the proceeding; or
if the evidence relates to the credibility of a child witness and is to be adduced in cross-examination of the child—the evidence has substantial probative value.
The evidence is not to be treated as being substantially relevant to facts in issue merely because of inferences it may raise as to the child witness’ or child complainant’s general disposition.
Without limiting the matters to which the court may have regard in deciding whether the evidence has substantial probative value, it is to have regard to:
whether the evidence tends to prove that the witness knowingly or recklessly made a false representation when the witness was under an obligation to tell the truth; and
the period that has elapsed since the acts or events to which the evidence relates were done or occurred.
This section does not apply if the child is a defendant in the proceeding.

section.heading: Leave under this Division

content.p: An application for leave under this Division:
must be in writing; and
if there is a jury in the proceeding in question—must be made in the jury’s absence; and
must not be determined before the court has considered such submissions and other evidence as it thinks necessary for determining the application.
If the court gives leave under this Division, the court must:
state its reasons in writing; and
cause those reasons to be entered in the court’s records.

section.heading: Disallowing inappropriate or aggressive cross-examination

content.p: The court may disallow a question put to a child witness in cross-examination in a proceeding if the question is inappropriate or unnecessarily aggressive.

In considering whether a question is inappropriate or unnecessarily aggressive, the court is to have regard to the child witness’ personal characteristics, including his or her age, culture, mental capacity and gender.

section.heading: Unrepresented defendants—cross-examination of child complainants

content.p: A defendant in a proceeding who is not represented by counsel is not to cross-examine a child complainant.
A person appointed by the court is to ask the child any questions that the defendant requests the person to ask the child.

section.heading: Unrepresented defendants—cross-examination of child witnesses

content.p: A defendant in a proceeding who is not represented by counsel is not to cross-examine a child witness (other than a child complainant), unless the court gives leave.
The court must not give leave unless satisfied that the child’s ability to testify under cross-examination will not be adversely affected if the defendant conducts the cross-examination.
In considering whether that ability will be adversely affected, the court is to have regard to any trauma that could be caused if the defendant conducts the cross-examination.
An application for leave under this section:
must be in writing; and
must not be determined before the court has considered such submissions and other evidence as it thinks necessary for determining the application.
If the court refuses leave, a person appointed by the court is to ask the child any questions that the defendant requests the person to ask the child.

section.heading: Represented defendants—cross-examination of child witnesses and child complainants

content.p: A defendant in a proceeding who is represented by counsel is not to cross-examine a child witness or a child complainant except through counsel.

division.heading: Special facilities for child witnesses to give evidence

section.heading: Closed-circuit television

content.p: A child witness’ evidence in a proceeding must be given by means of closed-circuit television unless:
the child is at least 16 and chooses not to give evidence by that means; or
the court orders that the child is not to give evidence by that means; or
the court is not equipped with facilities for evidence to be given by means of closed-circuit television.
Note: Section 15YL provides for alternative arrangements if a child witness does not give evidence by means of closed-circuit television.
The court must not make an order under paragraph (1)(b) unless satisfied that it is not in the interests of justice for the child witness’ evidence to be given by means of closed-circuit television.
This section does not affect the operation of any law in relation to the competence of a person to give evidence.

section.heading: Giving evidence by closed-circuit television

content.p: If the child witness’ evidence is given by means of closed-circuit television from a location outside a courtroom:
that location is taken to be part of the courtroom in which the proceeding is being held; and
the court may order that a court officer be present at that location; and
the court may order that another person be present with the child:
to act as an interpreter; or
to assist the child with any difficulty in giving evidence associated with a disability; or
to provide the child with other support.
An order under paragraph (1)(b) or (c) does not limit the operation of section 15YM.
The court may adjourn the proceeding, or a part of the proceeding, to a court or other place that is equipped with facilities for evidence to be given by means of closed-circuit television if:
the court is not equipped with facilities for evidence to be given by means of closed-circuit television; or
the court otherwise considers it appropriate to do so.

section.heading: Viewing evidence given by closed-circuit television

content.p: If the child witness’ evidence is given by means of closed-circuit television, the facilities used are to be operated in such a way that the people who have an interest in the proceeding can see the child, and any person present with the child, on one or more television monitors.

section.heading: Alternative arrangements for giving evidence

content.p: If a child witness’ evidence in a proceeding is not to be given by means of closed-circuit television, the court:
must make arrangements in order to restrict contact (including visual contact) that the child may have with any defendant while giving evidence; and
may make arrangements in order to restrict contact (including visual contact) that the child may have with members of the public while giving evidence.
The arrangements may include either of the following:
using screens;
planning seating arrangements for people who have an interest in the proceeding, including:
the level at which they are seated; and
the people in the child’s line of vision.
This section does not apply if the child is at least 16 and chooses not to give evidence under the arrangements.

section.heading: Use of video recordings

content.p: A video recording of an interview of a child witness in a proceeding may be admitted as evidence in chief if:
a constable, or a person of a kind specified in the regulations, conducted the interview; and
the court gives leave.
The court must not give leave if satisfied that it is not in the interest of justice for the child’s evidence in chief to be given by a video recording.
An application for leave under this section:
must be in writing; and
must not be determined before the court has considered such submissions and other evidence as it thinks necessary for determining the application.
The child witness must be available for cross-examination and re-examination if he or she gives evidence in chief by a video recording.
Note: Division 4 provides for this evidence to be given using closed-circuit television or other arrangements.

section.heading: Admissibility of evidence given using video recordings

content.p: The admissibility of the evidence given by video recording is not affected by the fact that it is evidence of previous representations that the child witness made in the interview that was being recorded.
Evidence given by video recording under section 15YM is not admissible if the court is satisfied that:
any defendant in the proceeding (other than the child witness if the child is a defendant); or
the defendant’s lawyer (if any);
was not given a reasonable opportunity to listen to and view the recording.
The court may refuse to admit the whole or part of the contents of a recording adduced as evidence under section 15YM.

section.heading: Adults accompanying child witnesses

content.p: A child witness may choose an adult to accompany the child while the child is giving evidence in a proceeding (including while giving evidence by closed-circuit television).
The adult so chosen may accompany the child as mentioned in subsection (1), unless the court determines that it is not appropriate for the adult to accompany the child.
The court may permit more than one adult to accompany the child if the court considers it in the interests of justice to do so.
An adult accompanying the child under this section must not:
prompt the child or otherwise influence the child’s answers; or
disrupt the questioning of the child.
Any words spoken by an adult accompanying the child under this section must be able to be heard by:
the judge; and
if there is a jury in the proceeding—the members of the jury.

section.heading: Exclusion of people from the courtroom

content.p: The court may order that some or all of the members of the public be excluded from the courtroom in which a child witness is giving evidence in a proceeding.

section.heading: Warnings etc. not to be given about children’s evidence

content.p: If there is a jury in a proceeding in which a child witness has given or will give evidence, the judge is not to warn the jury, or suggest to the jury in any way:
that the law regards children as an unreliable class of witness; or
that the law requires greater or lesser weight to be given to evidence that is given by closed-circuit television or alternative arrangements under Division 4; or
that the law requires greater or lesser weight to be given to evidence that is given by a video recording under Division 5; or
that the law requires greater or lesser weight to be given to evidence because an adult accompanies the child under section 15YO.

section.heading: Publication identifying child witnesses or child complainants

content.p: A person commits an offence if:
the person publishes any matter; and
the person does not have the leave of the court to publish the matter; and
the matter:
identifies another person (who is not a defendant in the proceeding) as a child witness or a child complainant in relation to the proceeding; or
is likely to lead to the other person being identified as such a child witness or child complainant.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 12 months, or 60 penalty units, or both.
This section does not apply if the publication is in:
an official publication in the course of, and for the purpose of, the proceeding; or
a document prepared for use in particular legal proceedings (whether or not the legal proceedings are a proceeding within the meaning of this Part).
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in subsection (2) (see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code).
The court may give leave to a person to publish the matter.
In deciding whether to give leave, the court is to have regard to:
any trauma to the child witness or child complainant that the publication could cause; and
any damage to the reputation of the child witness or child complainant that the publication could cause; and
whether the publication is:
for the purpose of supplying transcripts of the proceedings to persons with a genuine interest in the proceedings; or
for genuine research purposes.
Leave may be given after the proceedings have finished. For this purpose, the court need not be constituted by the same judicial officers who constituted the court in the proceedings.
An application for leave under this section:
must be in writing; and
must not be determined before the court has considered such submissions and other evidence as it thinks necessary for determining the application.

section.heading: General powers of a court

content.p: The power of a court to control the conduct of a proceeding is not affected by this Part, except so far as this Part provides otherwise expressly or by necessary intendment.
In particular, the powers of a court to control the questioning of witnesses are not affected.
The power of a court to give leave under this Part includes the power to give such leave subject to conditions.

section.heading: Division 5 of Part IIIA unaffected

content.p: Nothing in this Part affects the operation of Division 5 of Part IIIA (Child sex tourism—video link evidence).
